title: Accessibility of derived local equivalences in a combinatorial model category
statement: Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention] and the model-category, locally presentable and combinatorial terminology of [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a combinatorial model category with functorial factorizations, and let $S$ be a small set of its arrows. Use the original homotopy function complexes $\operatorname{Map}^h$ of [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping]. Call an originally fibrant object $Z$ local if $\operatorname{Map}^h(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(A,Z)$ is an equivalence for every $(A\to B)\in S$. Let $W_S$ be the full subcategory of the ordinary arrow category $\mathcal M^{[1]}$ whose objects are those $f:X\to Y$ for which $\operatorname{Map}^h(Y,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(X,Z)$ is an equivalence for every such local $Z$; morphisms in the arrow category are commuting squares. Then $W_S$ is replete, accessible, and accessibly embedded: for some infinite regular cardinal $\lambda$, it is closed under small $\lambda$-filtered colimits computed in $\mathcal M^{[1]}$ and is generated under those colimits by a small set of its objects. Replete means closed under isomorphisms in the arrow category. Here $\lambda$-filtered means that every diagram with fewer than $\lambda$ morphisms admits a cocone, and regular means that a union of fewer than $\lambda$ sets of size less than $\lambda$ has size less than $\lambda$. No left properness or simplicial enrichment is assumed, and the endpoints of the arrows of $S$ need not be cofibrant.
